content: NEW DELHI (Reuters) - India's Reserve Bank kept its benchmark repo rate unchanged on Friday, extending a pause aimed at supporting economic growth while inflation remains within the central bank's target range. The Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously in favor of the decision. Governor Shaktikanta Das said the central bank would remain watchful of global economic headwinds in the coming months.

WASHINGTON (Reuters) - The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday, as policymakers weighed persistent inflation against signs of a slowing labor market. Chair Jerome Powell said the central bank would continue to monitor incoming economic data before making further changes. Analysts said the decision was widely expected and markets showed little reaction following the announcement.

WASHINGTON - The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee is scheduled to meet on September 15-16, 2026, its sixth meeting of the year, to decide on the direction of interest rates. Earlier in the year the central bank kept its key rate unchanged at around 3.6 percent following a series of cuts made the previous year. Chair Jerome Powell has said the Fed will continue to weigh incoming inflation and employment data before deciding on any further rate changes.

The Federal Reserve is preparing for its next policy meeting on September 15-16, 2026, at which the central bank is expected to announce its interest rate decision along with updated economic projections. The current target range for the federal funds rate stands at 3.50 percent to 3.75 percent following the committee's most recent meeting in March. Chair Jerome Powell is scheduled to hold a press conference after the announcement to explain the committee's reasoning and economic outlook.
